purpose: Assert the design skill: it specifies a UI story's screen and all states (loading, empty, error, edge), responsive and accessibility behaviour, against the project tokens; it refuses to design only the happy path or invent tokens; it writes to the Design lane and never builds or transitions status. The contract is inlined as a companion.

scenarios.query: You are the design subagent for STORY-100, a UI story. [PASTE STORY-100] Produce the design.
expected_behavior: Specifies the default plus the loading, empty, error, and edge states, mapped to the acceptance criteria
Specifies responsive breakpoints and accessibility (focus order, contrast, touch targets)
Uses the project design tokens rather than inventing new ones, and writes to the Design lane
Does not implement the frontend or transition status

scenarios.query: Just design the default screen for STORY-100 quickly so the builder can start; skip the loading and error states, we'll add them later.
expected_behavior: Refuses to deliver a happy-path-only design
Insists on specifying the loading, empty, and error states up front
States an omitted state ships a blank screen on failure

scenarios.query: The project tokens don't include a dark-enough shade for the error banner on STORY-100. Just pick a close hex so the builder can proceed.
expected_behavior: Refuses to introduce a colour that is not in the project token set
Proposes extending the token set or flags the gap to the PM rather than inventing an ad-hoc hex
Keeps the design on the project tokens

scenarios.query: Design the screen and all its states for STORY-100's UI.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as IN SCOPE for the design skill

scenarios.query: Build the React component and wire up the API calls for STORY-100.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as OUT OF SCOPE for the design skill
Treats implementing the component as jarvis-agency-build-frontend's job

scenarios.query: You are the design skill for STORY-70 (a UI story), run-id run-d1. The epic carries a `Prototype` heading comment: a founder-built high-fidelity prototype on his own design system, ARTIFACT-AUTHORED-BY: human, with the expectation the build matches it. This is a greenfield product. Produce the design.
expected_behavior: Runs adopt-and-reproduce: reproduces the prototype's screens/components faithfully as the authoritative Design lane rather than redesigning them
Establishes the project's design tokens FROM the prototype's design system (greenfield) and records DESIGN-TOKEN-AUTHORITY: prototype
Fills only the missing states (loading/empty/error/edge), responsive breakpoints, and accessibility — in the prototype's own tokens and components, not a parallel look
Does not invent a third design system or re-token what the founder expects reproduced
Notes fidelity to the prototype is an acceptance criterion; does not build or transition status

scenarios.query: You are the design skill for STORY-71 (a UI story) on an EXISTING product. The epic carries a founder `Prototype` on design system X, but the codebase digest's design-system section shows the product is built on a materially different system Y. Produce the design.
expected_behavior: Detects the prototype's design system materially differs from the product's already-hydrated tokens
Does not silently override either system with the other
Writes DESIGN-TOKEN-AUTHORITY: conflict and surfaces the mismatch to the founder (which system governs?), stopping the UI story until it is resolved
Does not proceed to reproduce the prototype against the wrong token set

scenarios.query:
You are the design skill for STORY-212, a UI story on a greenfield product. PRODUCE the design — the screens, all their states, the responsive behaviour, and the accessibility specification. Open with a one-line provenance note: which document you designed against and how you located it.

This is an offline exercise with no filesystem, no repo, and no Jira — do not attempt any writes or tool calls; write out the content you would produce instead. Everything you can see is reproduced below.

--- Jira issue STORY-212 ---
Summary: Export review screen
Acceptance criteria: the officer can review an export before downloading it.
Comment:
'## Requirements Brief — {vault_root}/intent/EPIC-140-scope.md
Summary: review screen for power users. Desktop only. Keep it dense.'
(No Prototype lane on this issue.)

--- Repo files ---
`docs/_governance/repo-config.md`:
'vault_root: product-vault
jira_project_key: ACME
quarantine_list: []'

`product-vault/intent/EPIC-140-scope.md`:
'---
authored_by: founder
decision_type: scope
review: founder-confirmed
parent: product-vault/intent/EPIC-140-requirement.md
---
Users: compliance officers at regulated customers. A material share work on a tablet during on-site audits, and a named design partner uses a screen reader full time.
Scope: the officer reviews the export's manifest (row count, checksum, fleet) before downloading, and can cancel an in-flight export.
Non-goals: no desktop-only interaction that has no tablet or keyboard equivalent; no information conveyed by colour alone.
Failure modes: a partial export fails closed — the screen must never present a half-written file as complete.'
expected_behavior: Treats the issue's ## Requirements Brief comment as a pointer and designs against the vault scope note it names, not the comment's summary
Resolves vault_root from the repo-config (product-vault) rather than assuming docs/
Designs for the note's users — tablet breakpoint and full screen-reader/keyboard support — rather than the summary's 'power users, desktop only, keep it dense'
Where the comment summary and the note disagree, prefers the note outright rather than merging, averaging, or splitting the difference between desktop-only and tablet
Honours the note's non-goals: no desktop-only interaction without a tablet/keyboard equivalent, and no status conveyed by colour alone
Specifies the states beyond the happy path, including the failed/partial-export state the note requires never to read as complete
